ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a star-connected winding, with terminals labeled A, B, C, and the three windings joined at neutral point N; among them, the dot mark of the winding corresponding to A-N is near terminal A. On the right side is a delta-connected winding, with terminals labeled a, b, c; from the connection relationship in the figure, the delta side winding corresponding between a and b corresponds to the left-side A-N winding, and its dotted end is at terminal a. Reasoning: According to the transformer dot-marking convention, the secondary-side Vab is proportional to and in phase with the primary-side VAN. The given condition is negative-sequence voltage excitation, so VAN = 1∠0° and VBN = 1∠120° can be taken. The line voltage VAB = VAN - VBN = 1∠0° - 1∠120° = √3∠(-30°). Since Vab is in phase with VAN, the phase of VAB relative to Vab is -30°, that is, VAB lags Vab by 30°.

raw_record.question_text: If the star side of the star-delta transformer shown in the image is excited by a negative sequence voltage, how does \(V_{AB}\) relate in phase to \(V_{ab}\)?

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: identify the left side as the star side with phase winding A-N dotted at A, and identify the right delta side such that terminal voltage Vab is across the corresponding secondary winding with its dotted end at a. Use the transformer dot convention to set Vab proportional to and in phase with VAN. From the text, use that the excitation is negative sequence. Choose VAN = 1∠0 and VBN = 1∠120. Calculate VAB = VAN - VBN = √3∠(-30°). Compare this with Vab = k∠0; conclude VAB lags Vab by 30°.
